title: Prefill priming scheduler for mixed-burst workloads
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem statement: On mixed workloads that include short prefill+decode bursts and longer streaming sessions we observe suboptimal kernel choices and cold KV/cache behavior that inflate 95th percentile latency and unit cost. Existing kernel-advising logic focuses on per-request seqlen and static device profiles but does not proactively prime execution state when low-cost priming can avoid expensive fallbacks during bursts.

Goal: Implement a lightweight prefill priming scheduler that: 1) uses tiny, safe priming probes to warm relevant kernel paths and KV caches for an imminent burst; 2) budgets priming per-tenant and per-GPU to control cost; 3) integrates with the kernel advisor and online autotuner to bias kernel selection towards warmed/low-latency kernels for the duration of the burst; 4) provides safe rollback when priming harms latency/cost.

Scope: runtime scheduler + small probing client code + kernel-advisor signal extension + telemetry & dashboarding. Not in scope: new kernel implementations or low-level kernel micro-optimizations (we leverage those).
acceptance_criteria: A1: End-to-end prototype that issues priming probes prior to detected short bursts and records the priming lifecycle in telemetry (start, success/fail, kept/rolled-back)
A2: 95th percentile tail latency for short-prefill+decode burst workloads reduced by >=15% in lab mixed-load benchmark vs baseline with no priming
A3: Priming budget enforcement prevents monthly cost increase >2% for test tenants when enabled
A4: Kernel advisor receives priming-derived signals and demonstrates a measurable shift in kernel-choice distribution for primed bursts
A5: Feature gated and rollout plan with progressive ramp and rollback criteria documented in the PRD
tasks: T1: Design doc: describe probing sequence (micro-prefill microsamples), safety constraints, and metrics - Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RUNTIME/Prefill+Priming+Scheduler
T2: Implement priming client that generates tiny prefill requests (1-8 tokens synthetic prefixes) with tagging metadata
T3: Extend kernel-advisor API to accept priming-score and priming-timestamp signals
T4: Scheduler: priming budget manager, per-tenant rate limiter, priming retry/rollback policy
T5: Telemetry: add priming events to tracing, expose priming success/failure flags in Console route dashboards
T6: Offline perf experiments: run mixed-burst harness vs baseline, capture p50/p95/p99 + cost-per-token
T7: Safety/canary rollout plan and guardrails (circuit breaker for latency increase >10% on canary), PR review and testing
T8: Docs & SDK: document API flags and runtime config in developer docs and console feature flag
updates: 2025-02-14 - Aisha Patel: Created ticket after spike showing recurring p95 spikes on small-prefill traffic from two customers. Attached initial microbench notes and cost back-of-envelope.

2025-02-18 - Martin Schultz: Completed design spike. Prototype approach uses synthetic 4-token prefill probes targeted to hot routes; observed 12% p95 improvement on a 32-GPU test cluster when priming is applied selectively.

2025-02-22 - Martin Schultz: Added priming budget proposal. Default budget: 0.5% of tenant token budget or 500 priming probes / hour (whichever smaller). Need PM alignment on default and opt-in semantics.

2025-02-24 - Priya Nair (PM): Reviewed the design. PM concern: potential cross-tenant noise on shared GPUs. Action: add per-GPU isolation heuristic where priming is disabled if >60% of capacity already used.
2025-02-27 - Martin Schultz: Implemented initial telemetry events and a lightweight priming client in runtime branch. Running cluster-wide microbench; results uploaded to perf bucket.

2025-03-02 - Security review note (internal): No sensitive data in priming probes since they are synthetic prefixes. Add a review to ensure probes do not trigger model-level safety filters excessively.
2025-03-02 - Aisha Patel: Updated acceptance criteria to require cost gating and rollout plan. Moved status from Triage to Planned.
comments: Priya Nair (2025-02-19): Can we make priming tenant-configurable? Some enterprise customers may want to disable or require approval.
Martin Schultz (2025-02-20): Yes — expose as a tenant-level runtime flag. Default off for Dedicated private installs unless enabled by the admin.
Ravi Kapoor (Infra, 2025-02-25): Watch out for KV cache explosion if priming volume is high across many tenants. Recommend LRU trimming policy for primed keys.
Elena Rossi (SRE, 2025-03-01): Add canary metric to detect tail-latency regressions within 5 minutes of enabling; automated rollback should trigger if p95 increases >10% on canary group.
